title: Detection and enumeration of Lak megaphages in microbiome samples by PCR
author: Crisci, Corsini, et al.
materials: Validated procedure for DNA extraction using PowerFecal Pro DNA kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany) on a range of microbiome samples, including feces/solid digesta, mucosal tissues and fluid digesta. Follow manufacturer instructions with adaptations as below:1.Lysis.a.Mix solid samples in collection tubes with a sterile spatula.b.Place approximately 0.25 g of solid sample in a bead tube with 800 μL lysis buffer.i.For liquid samples, use 200 μL of sample with 600 μL lysis buffer.c.Heat tubes at 65°C for 10 min, using a water bath or heat block.Note: Heating will aid disassembly of the phage capsid and the release of genetic material.d.Using a vortex adapter, vortex tubes for 10 min at maximum speed.2.Inhibitor removal and washing (as specified in manufacturer instructions)3.Elution.a.Use 60 μL of elution buffer and incubate spin column at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 10 min.i. Centrifuge at 13,000 ×g for 1 min.ii. Once eluted, pass the same 60 μL eluate back through the same spin column (without incubation) and repeat centrifugation.4.Measure DNA concentration by UV spectrophotometry.5.Store DNA at −20°C until analysis.

Timing: 2 h
11.Presence of Lak phage in microbiome DNA can be visualized using agarose gel electrophoresis.12.Purified PCR products can be sequenced for confirmation and comparison. We recommend using either QIAquick PCR purification or gel extraction kits (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany) prior to sequencing. To maximise yield, follow manufacturer instructions with adaptations as below:a.Use 30 μL of elution buffer and incubate spin column at room temperature for 10 min.b.Centrifuge at 13,000 ×g for 1 min.c.Once eluted, pass the same 30 μL eluate back through the same spin column (without incubation) and repeat centrifugation.13.Measure DNA concentration by UV spectrophotometry.
CRITICAL: PCR purification of Lak MCP gene amplicons is a prerequisite in generating standards for the following qPCR assay.

steps.title: Extract DNA from microbiome samples
steps.instruction: Use the PowerFecal Pro DNA kit (Qiagen) with the following adaptations:

substeps.instruction: Lysis: Mix solid samples in collection tubes with a sterile spatula; place ~0.25 g solid sample in a bead tube with 800 µL lysis buffer (for liquid samples use 200 µL sample + 600 µL lysis buffer). Heat tubes at 65 °C for 10 min (water bath or heat block). Vortex tubes for 10 min at maximum speed using a vortex adapter.
Inhibitor removal and washing: Follow the manufacturer’s instructions.

Elution: Add 60 µL elution buffer to the spin column, incubate at room temperature (20 °C–22 °C) for 10 min, then centrifuge at 13,000 ×g for 1 min. Pass the same 60 µL eluate back through the same spin column (no incubation) and centrifuge again at 13,000 ×g for 1 min.

steps.title: Measure extracted DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Determine DNA concentration using UV spectrophotometry.

steps.title: Store extracted DNA
steps.instruction: Aliquot and keep the DNA at –20 °C until further analysis.

steps.title: Visualize Lak phage PCR products
steps.instruction: Run the PCR amplicons on an agarose gel electrophoresis system to confirm presence of Lak phage.

steps.title: Purify PCR amplicons for sequencing
steps.instruction: Purify the Lak MCP gene amplicons using QIAquick PCR purification or gel extraction kits (Qiagen) with the following adaptations:

substeps.instruction: Add 30 µL elution buffer to the spin column, incubate at room temperature for 10 min, then centrifuge at 13,000 ×g for 1 min.
Pass the same 30 µL eluate back through the same spin column (no incubation) and centrifuge again at 13,000 ×g for 1 min.

steps.title: Measure purified PCR DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Quantify the purified PCR product using UV spectrophotometry.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of qPCR data
steps.instruction: Analyze qPCR results using the workflow below:

substeps.instruction: Prepare data: Collate all variables into a table, calculate averages for technical replicates, and log‑transform the values.
Analyze distribution: Perform group‑wise distribution analysis, identify outliers (JMP® defines outliers as 1.5 × IQR) and remove them if needed.
Design statistical model: Use least‑squared‑means comparisons or ANOVA where feasible; include covariates such as sex, age, or location.
Means separation: For >2 group comparisons apply Tukey’s HSD test; for two‑group comparisons use a t‑test or equivalent.

description: The protocol below describes specific steps for processing and screening fecal, digesta and mucosal samples for Lak phages, but can be adapted for different sample types. We have also implemented the protocol for use with liquid samples (e.g., jejunal and rumen fluid) and mucosal brushes suspended in sodium-magnesium (SM) buffer.
